title: Claude Code produces the first primary Lund jet-plane density measurement in electron–positron collisions
summary: A Claude Code agent pipeline analyzed archived 1994 ALEPH hadronic-Z data and reported the first primary Lund jet-plane density measurement in e⁺e⁻ collisions. Its unfolded 57-bin fiducial result shows the expected triangular QCD radiation structure and a shallow low-transverse-momentum turnover; the integrated mean primary-emission count is 4.751 ± 0.224 per hemisphere. This is one new measurement, not a claim of discovering new particles or physics beyond QCD.
ai_technology: Claude Code agents orchestrated by the Just Furnish Context (JFC) framework
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions; CERN; ALEPH Collaboration archival data

evidence.tested: A Claude Code agent pipeline analyzed archived 1994 ALEPH hadronic-Z data and reported the first primary Lund jet-plane density measurement in e⁺e⁻ collisions.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint, and the authors explicitly qualify the novel measurement as subject to independent verification. It uses 1994 ALEPH data and one available full-simulation sample; the corrected density is prior/model dependent, with a reported 6.0% density-weighted total uncertainty and 4.7% uncertainty on the integrated count. The shallow residual shape is within current generator-theory uncertainty, so the paper frames it as a benchmark rather than evidence excluding generators.
evidence.ai_role: Agents planned and executed the event selection, jet declustering, unfolding, uncertainty propagation, statistical checks and report drafting using archived ALEPH data and literature retrieval. The paper attributes the new Lund-plane measurement to an autonomous AI-agent analysis pipeline; human authors supplied the broad task and review framework.
